title: Geometrically normal tensor normal domains
statement: Let k : Type u be a field [def-weil-field], and let A : Type v and B : Type w be commutative k-algebras which are normal domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Assume geometric normality of A is tested on every field extension E/k [def-pc-field-extension] with E : Type (max u v w): each A tensor_k E is normal. Then A tensor_k B is normal. Tensor products are the commutative tensor-product algebras [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The common test universe includes the fraction fields of both algebras and the lifted subalgebras used in the proof.

source.place: Tag 06DF, reduction to normal domains and finite-type tensor argument

proof.text: Lift A and B to the common universe, transporting along the ULift algebra equivalences at the end. For each finite-type k-subalgebra D of B, its integral closure N in Frac(D) is finite over D by Noether finiteness (the degree-one fraction-field extension). Embed Frac(D) in Frac(B). Elements of N are integral over B, so lie in B by integral closedness. The image is a normal finite-type subalgebra containing D. These images form a nonempty directed cover of B. The tensor-product universal property explicitly constructs the colimit cocone; normality of filtered colimits reduces to finite-type normal B.

Put K=Frac(A) and L=Frac(B). Scalar extension commutes with localization, so K remains geometrically normal. A normal ring is reduced: its localizations at maximal ideals are domains, and reducedness is local. Thus all K tensor_k E are reduced. In positive characteristic use geometric reducedness to obtain separability; in characteristic zero use separable generation over the perfect base field.

Use the declared directed cover of the separable field K by smooth finite-type subalgebras D. Base change makes B tensor_k D smooth over the normal ring B, hence normal. The explicit tensor-product colimit cocone and filtered-colimit normality show K tensor_k B is normal. Separately A tensor_k L is normal by geometric normality.

Write C=A tensor_k B and S=K tensor_k B. Tensor maps induced by injections of vector spaces are injective, so C embeds in S. Hence C is reduced, since S is normal. The ring S is finite type over K, so Noetherian and has finitely many minimal primes. For any injective ring map, every minimal prime of the source is the contraction of a minimal prime of the target: the comap of the zero ideal is zero and minimal-prime comap covers its minimal primes (Mathlib Ideal.minimalPrimes_comap_subset). Thus C has finitely many minimal primes; no going-down theorem is used.

The tensor maps C to S=K tensor_k B and U=A tensor_k L are injective localizations. Injectivity implies each inverted element is a nonzerodivisor. Embed S and U in Q(C), and embed T=K tensor_k L there by one more localization; the latter map is injective. The two embeddings of C agree by the localization universal property. Any x in Q(C) integral over C is integral over S and U. Localizing Q(C) also identifies it as the total fractions of S and U, so their normality puts x in both images.

For the intersection, split the injective k-linear map f:A to K by a linear retraction p. If a in K tensor B and b in A tensor L have equal images in K tensor L, set z=(p tensor id)(a). Tensor functoriality and p composed with f=id show that z maps to b in A tensor L. Injectivity of id_K tensor(B to L) then shows that z maps to a in K tensor B. Apply this to the two representatives of x from the previous step, obtaining x in C. Thus C is integrally closed in Q(C). The reduced, finite-minimal-prime normality criterion proves C is normal. Transport from the universe lifts to the original algebras.

lean.statement:
theorem normal_domain_case
    {k : Type u} {A : Type v} {B : Type w}
    [Field k] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra k A] [Algebra k B] [IsDomain A] [IsIntegrallyClosed A]
    [IsDomain B] [IsIntegrallyClosed B]
    (hA : ∀ (E : Type (max u v w)) [Field E] [Algebra k E],
      ∀ (p : Ideal (A ⊗[k] E)) [p.IsPrime],
        IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p))
    (hB : ∀ (p : Ideal B) [p.IsPrime],
      IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p)) :
    ∀ (p : Ideal (A ⊗[k] B)) [p.IsPrime],
      IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p)

statement_change.old_statement: Let k be a field and A,B commutative k-algebras which are normal domains. If A is geometrically normal over k, then A tensor_k B is a normal ring.
statement_change.what: Repair the elaborated Lean universes: an independent Type* for E could test a smaller universe with no field extension of the base. Use E : Type (max u v w), as in the unchanged main theorem, so the fraction fields used by Tag 06DF are among the tests. The mathematical statement is unchanged. This stage-3 interface repair also spells out the corrected universe scope in the natural-language statement.

old_proof.text: Use finite-type normal subalgebra extensions and the filtered tensor-product colimit to reduce B to finite type. The fraction field of A is separable by geometric reducedness; express it as a filtered colimit of smooth subalgebras. Smooth base change over the normal domain B is normal, and localization identifies the stages. The finite-type case then follows from the total-fraction-ring intersection argument and the reduced normal characterization.
